subject: Segmentation justification & routing matrix for Acme - evidence pack requested
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acme-fin.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <sec-req@acme-fin.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation, routing details requested for SOC2/CAIQ review

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Our security folks asked for a concise justification of the network segmentation strategy you recommend for Dedicated and Private deployments, plus a routing matrix that ties each zone to the controls we need to validate for SOC 2 and CAIQ (for example: control plane isolation, tenant data plane isolation, egress controls, and interconnect behavior).

Can you provide: 1) a short architecture justification (one page) explaining why the segmentation model is safe for multi-tenant Dedicated and for VPC-private installs; 2) a CSV-style routing matrix showing source zone, destination, protocol/ports, firewall rules, and whether the path uses NAT/peering/transit; and 3) any sample ACLs or firewall snippets you can share?

If you have an internal diagram or checklist you can attach that would accelerate our review. We need this for an internal assessment next Wednesday (06/30).

Appreciate it,
Lydia Chen
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Financial

---

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation, routing details requested for SOC2/CAIQ review

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short justification, a routing matrix CSV, and an ACL summary PDF. High level:

- Model overview: Redwood uses a layered isolation model. Control plane services (management, model registry, tenant metadata) live in a dedicated control VPC/subnet with strictly limited ingress (company mgmt IPs + private peering).
- Data plane: customer inference workloads run in tenant-specific compute pools. For Dedicated, tenants can be assigned physical or logical isolation (GPU pools + tenant VPCs). For Private (VPC or on-prem), we recommend host-level network namespaces with per-tenant subnets and eBPF-based microsegmentation where available.
- Interconnects: we support three routing patterns: direct VPC peering (low-latency, private IPs), private interconnect (MPLS/colocation VLAN), and NATed egress through a controlled egress VPC. Peering is used for private deployments; Dedicated tenants may use NAT or an assigned public egress IP depending on compliance.
- Egress & logging: all egress flows are funnelled through an egress cluster with per-tenant IP tagging, NAT translation if required, and full packet-level logging forwarded to the customer-configured SIEM or our managed logging collector (retention policy is configurable).

I called out where controls map to CAIQ/SIG sections in the justification doc (Control plane separation, Network boundary, egress controls). See attachments for the routing matrix (CSV) and the diagram (PNG).

Deliverables attached: 20260628_segmentation-diagram.png, 20260628_routing-matrix.csv, 20260628_acl-summaries.pdf

Let us know if you want a redline-friendly version of the ACLs. If acceptable, we can also add a per-tenant NAT example showing SNAT rules for Azure/GCP/AWS.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Segmentation, routing details requested for SOC2/CAIQ review

Lydia — quick follow-up from product re: a few items your auditors typically ask for. Can you confirm whether your assessment requires:

- Per-tenant NAT translation examples (we can provide AWS/GCP/Azure SNAT snippets)
- Explicit control-plane peering ACLs (we have a minimal allow-list used for control plane health checks)
- Proof of microsegmentation enforcement (we can provide iptables/eBPF policy excerpts and an evidence screenshot showing enforcement counters)

If you confirm, I’ll append those to the packet. Timeline: we can add the NAT and control-plane ACLs by EOD Friday 06/26 and the enforcement evidence by Monday 06/29.

Marissa Cole
Product Security Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Segmentation, routing details requested for SOC2/CAIQ review

Lydia — confirming we uploaded the additional artifacts to the secure folder and included mapping to common CAIQ/SIG controls. Summary of what's in the folder: 

1) segmentation-diagram.png — annotated zones: Control Plane, Management, Tenant Data Plane, Egress Cluster, Monitoring/Logging. Diagram shows allowed flows and default-deny boundaries.
2) routing-matrix.csv — row per flow: source_zone,dest_zone,protocol,ports,firewall_action,nat,log_forwarding,example_acl_id
3) acl-summaries.pdf — human-readable ACL snippets for control plane peering, tenant-to-egress, and cross-tenant deny rules.
4) evidence/ — enforcement screenshots and iptables/eBPF policy excerpts (redacted).

Control mappings included: CAIQ Network Security (NET) mapping, SOC 2 CC6 (system and communications protection) crosswalk, and SIG item references for routing controls.

Next steps: If your team needs an on-call window to review the enforcement screenshots with one of our infra engineers, ping a couple of suggested times and we’ll schedule. Otherwise we can prepare a tailored appendix that highlights differences between Dedicated physical-pool isolation and private VPC isolation for vendor review.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Security — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
